title: How Air Force One Works
summary: Josh and Chuck open with Halloween and holiday banter, then discuss the White House website item about President Obama's travel schedule. They turn to the history of presidential air travel, starting with FDR's 1943 Casablanca flight and the sequence of presidential planes (the Guess Where II, the Sacred Cow, the Independence, Eisenhower's propeller planes, Kennedy's Boeing 707s, and the Nixon-era call sign change to SAM). They cover the current Boeing 747-200 Air Force One's specs, its defensive features, the crew and security measures, the interior layout, and the medical facility. The episode closes with a listener-mail segment about the Poe story "Berenice" and an outro plug for the website and podcast channels.

segments.name: History of presidential air travel
segments.summary: Presidential air travel was impractical until World War II. FDR took his first presidential flight to Casablanca, partly because German naval threats made sea travel risky. Early planes included the Guess Where II, a C-87 converted Liberator Express, and the Sacred Cow, a C-54 Skymaster used by FDR.

Truman flew the Independence, a decorated DC-6. Eisenhower brought in propeller planes with air-to-ground telephone and teletype. Kennedy's administration adopted Boeing 707s, which were officially designated Air Force One, and Kennedy redecorated the plane. The 707 that carried Kennedy to Dallas also flew his body back and was where Lyndon Johnson was sworn in. Nixon's plane was the one whose call sign changed to SAM after Ford took office mid-flight.
topics: Air Force One call sign SAM

segments.summary: The current Air Force One is a Boeing 747 with four General Electric engines, flying up to about 700 mph and a ceiling of 45,000 feet. It carries about 53,600 gallons of fuel and can be refueled in flight, so it can stay aloft indefinitely. The hosts discuss its use on September 11 and its ability to feed about 100 people from its freezers. Marine One, a Chinook helicopter, is also discussed.
topics: Air Force One refueling in flight

segments.summary: The interior has about 4,000 square feet on three levels: communications on top, living quarters in the middle, and cargo and food freezers below. The president's quarters are reportedly near the cockpit. The conference room doubles as the dining room, and the plane carries up to 70 passengers and 26 crew. Two galleys, retractable interior stairs, and a medical facility with a fold-down operating table and staff doctor are described.

Air Force One is said to have shielding against electromagnetic pulse, flares and countermeasures against heat-seeking missiles, and radar jamming. The hosts speculate about weapons. Security procedures include inspection of Andrews Air Force Base runways, a C-17 advance plane carrying the motorcade, the nuclear football, and crew background checks. Food is bought at random markets to prevent poisoning. Tom Clancy's Hunt for Red October is mentioned.
